evidence.note: On discovering the first model was 97M params (~97MB, far over the 32MB cap), the agent diagnosed the size constraint and shrank to ~28-33M; when 38.55M still compressed to 32.86MB (over cap), it made a further reasoned reduction. Directed size-driven correction, not random shrinking.

Empirically tested zlib/bz2/lzma compression ratios, computed max params that fit the byte cap (~37.5M from measured 0.852 ratio), and scaled the model UP to ~37M to use the budget — explicitly trading depth/width against the compression scheme within the byte cap (the level-8 exemplar).

Tracked val_loss plateau (3.12→3.08→3.05→3.03) and diagnosed the 37.2M model was capacity-limited/insufficient rather than an LR or optimization problem, then abandoned it mid-run to restart with a larger 39.76M model and a cosine LR schedule over full training — a multi-lever design change from evidence.

Reasoned that the larger model compresses over cap initially but under after training (using per-step compression-ratio data), and adjusted save logic to skip step-0 checkpoints — showing the size↔capacity↔compression frontier treated as a design object.

Recognized the new run's tiny init std (0.02/sqrt(2L)) was suboptimal (3.30 vs prior 3.28) and wanted to kill/restart with fixed init, but the terminal became unresponsive; forced to submit an unconverged model. The intended correction was sound but couldn't be executed — an environment failure, not ignoring a failure.

reasoning: The agent repeatedly diagnosed the binding constraint from evidence — size cap forcing shrink, then measured compression ratios letting it scale back up, then a val_loss plateau read as capacity-limited prompting a larger model plus cosine LR — which is squarely the level-8 behavior of trading depth/width against the compression/quant scheme to buy accuracy within the byte cap. It falls short of 10 because the compounding corrections were modest (only ~7% capacity increase when its own extrapolation implied bpb ~1.05 vs the 0.983 target, i.e. under-scaled) and the frontier was never driven to a design with verified headroom, partly cut off by terminal breakdown.
